record.original_question: Can one construct a unified seminorm framework that interpolates between the total-oscillation seminorm and the exponentially weighted Fourier-coefficient seminorm used in Theorem 4.3, in order to prove spr(P)<1 on a domain containing both the disc given by inequality (4.5) and the real interval [0,1/(Delta-1))?

evidence.quote: The question is: How to interpolate smoothly between these two radically different seminorms ... in order to prove spr(P) < 1 for a domain DDelta containing both the disc (4.5) and the interval [0, 1/(Delta - 1) )?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Delta \ge 2$ be an integer and consider the $q$-coloring (zero-temperature antiferromagnetic Potts) model on rooted trees of maximum degree $\Delta$. For a complex parameter $\lambda$ (or, equivalently, $q$) one defines a recursion/transfer operator $P = P_\lambda$ acting on a space of generating functions (or measures) on single-vertex marginals at the root, whose iteration encodes the recursive computation of the partition function on a $\Delta$-regular branching tree. The spectral radius condition $\operatorname{spr}(P_\lambda) < 1$ implies uniqueness of the Gibbs measure / decay of correlations.

Two seminorms have been used to establish $\operatorname{spr}(P_\lambda) < 1$ in different regimes:

(a) A total-oscillation seminorm $\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{osc}}$, which yields $\operatorname{spr}(P_\lambda) < 1$ on the real interval
$$\lambda \in \Bigl[0,\ \tfrac{1}{\Delta - 1}\Bigr).$$

(b) An exponentially weighted Fourier-coefficient seminorm $\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{Fou}}$, which (via a theorem of the form "Theorem 4.3") yields $\operatorname{spr}(P_\lambda) < 1$ on a complex disc
$$D_{(4.5)} = \{\lambda \in \mathbb{C} : |\lambda| < r(\Delta)\}$$
for an explicit radius $r(\Delta)$.

The two seminorms are of qualitatively different nature, and neither one alone covers the union of these two regions.

\textbf{Problem.} Construct a one-parameter family of seminorms $\|\cdot\|_t$, $t \in [0,1]$, that interpolates smoothly between $\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{osc}}$ (at $t=0$) and $\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{Fou}}$ (at $t=1$), and use it to prove
$$\operatorname{spr}(P_\lambda) < 1 \quad\text{for all } \lambda \in \mathcal{D}_\Delta,$$
where $\mathcal{D}_\Delta \subset \mathbb{C}$ is a connected open domain containing both the disc $D_{(4.5)}$ and the real interval $[0, \tfrac{1}{\Delta - 1})$.
artifact.category_tag: transfer operators for hard-core / Potts models on trees
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not surface a follow-up paper that explicitly constructs the requested interpolating family of seminorms unifying the total-oscillation and exponentially weighted Fourier-coefficient approaches for proving spr(P) < 1 on a domain containing both the complex disc and the real interval [0, 1/(Δ−1)). The status is therefore unverified from available sources.
